name: Emerson
summary: Emerson publishes several compatible machinery monitoring paths. AMS 9420 and AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor are distinct WirelessHART devices; AMS Machine Works can receive both. AMS Optics is the current name for Plantweb Optics. These are product relationships, not a mandated single deployment.

flows.name: AMS 9420 wireless vibration route

steps.label: AMS 9420 transmitter
steps.detail: Collects vibration and temperature; the 2025 data sheet identifies this device separately from the newer monitor.

steps.label: WirelessHART gateway
steps.detail: IEC 62591 mesh reaches an Emerson Smart Wireless Gateway, which manages paths.

steps.label: AMS analysis software
steps.detail: AMS Machinery Manager or AMS Machine Works can store and analyze AMS 9420 vibration data.

steps.label: Machinery diagnosis
steps.detail: AMS software supports trending, alerts and fault diagnosis; no specific enterprise workflow is implied.

flows.caveat: DeltaV, Ovation and third-party hosts are supported alternatives, not required hops in this route.

flows.name: Current AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor route

steps.label: Wireless Vibration Monitor
steps.detail: Triaxial vibration and temperature sensing with PeakVue Plus prescriptive indications.

steps.label: WirelessHART mesh
steps.detail: Compatible with existing WirelessHART networks and AMS 9420 installations.

steps.label: AMS Machine Works
steps.detail: Emerson names this as one supported system for deeper waveform and spectrum diagnosis.

steps.label: AMS machinery workflow
steps.detail: Machine Works offers machinery analysis, routes and case management; AMS Optics is a separate enterprise collaboration option.

flows.caveat: Emerson also lists DeltaV, AMS Optics, historians and other integrations; this path is illustrative, not a required full stack.

findings.assessment: These are separate products. Emerson describes compatibility between their installations and lists both independently in AMS Machine Works.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §3: Plantweb Optics as the enterprise product name
findings.assessment: Emerson announced the transition of Plantweb Optics to AMS Optics in August 2023.
AspenTech became a wholly owned Emerson subsidiary on 12 March 2025. Mtell's inclusion does not establish that every AMS deployment passes through Mtell.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §3: AMS 6500 ATG is protection-class hardware
findings.assessment: Emerson describes AMS 6500 ATG as an API 670-compliant protection system with embedded prediction technology; it is a separate wired option.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §3: current AMS Machine Works version is v1.8
findings.assessment: The archived version is time-bound. Emerson's current article discusses v2.0, so the version should not be used as a timeless product label.

unknowns: Exact site network segmentation, server placement and software configuration vary by deployment and are not established by these product pages.
A direct, required data path from AMS Machine Works or AMS Optics into Aspen Mtell is not established here.
